description: I am tackling the AstroVital challenge as a focused, solo researcher. Operating independently allows me to rapidly iterate, skip project management overhead, and build a streamlined solution dedicated to improving life-support metrics, astronaut health tracking, or physiological environmental data translation.
summary:
ASTROVITAL is an offline-capable astronaut health and wellbeing dashboard prototype for long-duration space missions. It combines two complementary layers: AstroVitals, for crew-entered physiological observations and mission-day records, and AyurSpace, an optional
Ayurveda-inspired, non-clinical wellness reflection layer.

The integrated prototype brings together manually entered heart rate, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), sleep and fatigue observations; daily water and food intake; work, exercise, sleep and rest routines; mission environment and exposure records (space station, spacecraft transit, spacewalk/EVA and planetary-surface activity); and mood, stress and energy check-ins approximately every 12 hours. A mission overview displays recent entries and transparent, illustrative review prompts.

AyurSpace adds optional reflections inspired by Dinacharya (daily activities), Ahara and Agni (food and digestive comfort), Nidra (sleep and recovery), and Manas (mood and perceived stress). Tridosha concepts are presented only as traditional cultural lenses. They are not
biomarkers, diagnoses or validated spaceflight measurements. 

All sample values are synthetic and all new records are manually entered and stored locally in the browser. The prototype does not connect to NASA telemetry, sensors or astronaut medical records. It is intended to explore structured self-observation and communication—not to diagnose, prescribe or make mission decisions.
details:
The problem

Long-duration space missions create a complex environment in which physiological observations, sleep-wake patterns, nutrition, hydration, workload, physical activity, mission exposure and psychological wellbeing may all matter. A crew-friendly way to record these domains together may help astronauts review their own patterns and communicate observations to authorised support teams.

What the integrated ASTROVITAL prototype does

  1. AstroVitals - physiological observations: manual entries for heart rate, SpO₂, sleep duration, fatigue rating and activity context. Recent observations appear in the overview.
  2. Ilustrative trend and review prompts: displays recent manually entered readings and simple, transparent demonstration prompts based on broad example rules. These are not clinical thresholds, diagnoses, risk predictions or autonomous alerts. No prompt establishes fitness for duty or replaces mission procedures.
  3. Daily intake log: records water volume, number of food/meal entries, optional food summary and self-reported appetite/ digestive comfort. It does not prescribe a hydration target or diet.
  4. Work, activity and rest log: Records mission duty hours, exercise/activity and sleep/rest hours.
  5. Mission environment and exposure log: records context such as space station/orbital habitat, spacecraft transit, planetary surface, lunar surface or Mars surface; activity types include routine habitat operations, spacewalk/EVA, planetary surface EVA and recovery; duration is recorded where relevant.
  6. 12-hour mood check-in: supports start- and end-of-wakingperiod (AM/PM) self-reports of mood, perceived stress and energy/alertness, with an optional note. These are subjective selfreports, not psychological assessments.
  7. AyurSpace: a separate optional reflection layer using Dinacharya, Ahara, Agni, Nidra and Manas. Vata/Pitta/Kapha are described only as traditional lenses for reflection—not medical categories, biomarkers or validated space-health indicators.
  8. Crew log and export: records are stored in the current browser using localStorage and can be exported as CSV.

How it works

The prototype is a single-page HTML5, CSS3 and vanilla JavaScript application. Users manually enter observations through forms. The dashboard updates and stores records in browser local Storage. It works locally without an account, server or network connection. It has no live sensors, no live telemetry, no NASA API connection, no multi-user account system and no clinical decision model.

Benefits and hoped-for outcomes

ASTROVITAL explores whether combining physiological observations with daily routine, intake, mission exposure and periodic mood check-ins can make self-observation more structured and support communication. AyurSpace tests whether an optional culturally informed reflection layer can complement—but remain clearly separate from—space-medicine monitoring. These potential benefits require usability research and evaluation with astronauts, clinicians, behavioural-health specialists and human-factors experts.

Tools and technologies

HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript, browser localStorage and browsergenerated CSV export. No external code library, live NASA API or external data service is used in the current prototype.

Current limitations

All preloaded values are synthetic. Physiological entries are manual demonstration values, not sensor measurements. Review prompts use illustrative rules and are not medically validated. Water, food, work and rest entries are descriptive records, not recommended targets. Mood and fatigue ratings are subjective self-reports. Local browser storage is not an approved secure system for real astronaut health information. The application has not been validated for operational or clinical use.
dataRefs: NASA Human Research Program — Risks of Human Spaceflight
